extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, researchers, and editors interested in the Bhopal disaster or industrial-disaster articles
extracted.subtask_description: Writing or evaluating a comprehensive Wikipedia-style encyclopedic article about an industrial disaster, covering background, timeline, causes, impacts, legal outcomes, remediation, and references. Focus is on completeness, sourcing, neutrality, and structure for a long-form reference entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infobox and lead summary completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a concise lead and an infobox summarising key facts (Date, Time, Location, Also known as, Type, Cause, Deaths, Non-fatal injuries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article begins with an infobox listing Date, Time, Location, Also known as, Type, Cause, Deaths, and Non-fatal injuries — these fields should be filled with sourced values. The lead should summarise the event, scale (e.g., 'what is considered the world's worst industrial disaster'), and major outcomes. Anti-pattern: a lead or infobox missing key quantitative facts or using unsourced estimates without attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide precise citations and page references
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite reliable sources for claims and provide page numbers for existing citations where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page displays a maintenance note: 'This article cites its sources but does not provide page references. Please help improve it by providing page numbers for existing citations.' Scoring guidance: articles with full inline citations including page numbers and direct links to sources rate higher. Anti-patterns: unsourced statements, broad claims without citation, or reliance on a single secondary source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive background on facility and processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the plant's history, ownership, production processes (chemical reactions, intermediates), and operational context leading up to the incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article provides details such as UCIL plant construction date, MIC production added in 1979, and chemical process steps (methylamine + phosgene -> MIC -> reaction with 1-naphthol). Good coverage explains why the plant's process differed from others, production/stockpiling context, and prior safety incidents. Anti-pattern: superficial background that omits technical process details or ownership structure that affect liability analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed chronology and timeline of the incident
rubrics_metrics.description: Present a clear, time-stamped narrative of the incident (when leaks were detected, readings, employee actions, alarm activation, public warning), including specific times and sequence of events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article records times (e.g., 10:30 p.m., 11 p.m., 11:45 p.m., 12:40 a.m., 12:50 a.m., ~2 a.m.) and describes the escalation from instrumentation readings to alarm decoupling and public siren being silenced. Good articles use primary-source or investigation reports for the timeline and note discrepancies between accounts. Anti-pattern: vague timelines ('that night') or contradictory time claims without reconciliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical analysis of causes and contributing safety failures
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain immediate technical cause(s) (e.g., water entry into MIC tank, runaway exothermic reaction) and enumerate failed or inadequate safety systems (refrigeration, flare tower, vent-gas scrubbers, alarms, pressure gauges).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article lists malfunctioning systems, undersized devices, disconnected alarms, inactive refrigeration, and contaminated or corroded piping. It distinguishes hypotheses (e.g., accidental water ingress vs. deliberate sabotage) and cites investigations. Good coverage presents multiple inquiry findings and identifies areas of uncertainty. Anti-pattern: asserting a single cause without acknowledging alternative theories or lacking source attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantified immediate and long-term health impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Report casualty figures, injury counts, cohort studies, and documented long-term health effects (respiratory, ocular, neurological, reproductive, increased mortality/morbidity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article includes multiple figures (e.g., 'At least 3,787; over 16,000 claimed', government affidavit of 558,125 injuries) and describes long-term clinical findings and cohort follow-up limitations (loss to follow-up, bias). Good practice: present ranges, note differing estimates and their sources, and summarise study quality and gaps. Anti-pattern: presenting a single contested number as definitive or omitting study limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal, criminal, and compensation coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Document civil and criminal proceedings, settlement amounts, convictions, extradition efforts, and legislation created in the aftermath (e.g., Bhopal Gas Leak Disaster Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article outlines UCC's $470 million 1989 settlement, subsequent court rulings transferring suits to India, convictions in 2010, and later legal developments (appeals, dismissals). It should include dates, courts, and legal rationales. Anti-pattern: incomplete legal timeline or missing major rulings and settlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental contamination and remediation description
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe soil and groundwater contamination, lists of pollutants found or alleged, waste-handling decisions, cleanup actions, and disputes over remedial responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article names reported contaminants (1-naphthol, mercury, chromium, HCH, organochlorines) and documents remediation efforts, court orders for disposal, and controversies (state vs. corporation responsibility). Good coverage cites environmental studies and court decisions. Anti-pattern: vague statements about 'pollution' without specifics or sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Socioeconomic rehabilitation and compensation detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Record government relief measures, compensation amounts, pension schemes, employment programmes, housing plans, and evaluations of their adequacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the article include interim relief amounts, widow pensions, number of registered/awarded/rejected cases, and programmes like work-sheds and 'widow's colony'. Provide figures, implementation status, criticisms, and outcomes where known. Anti-pattern: listing programmes without indicating scale, timeline, or whether they succeeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutral tone, balance of perspectives, and marking of uncited claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Present a neutral, balanced narrative, attribute viewpoints (company, government, activists, researchers), and flag claims lacking sources (e.g., with 'citation needed').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article contains critical commentary (e.g., 'campaign of erasure') but also documents company positions and differing theories. It uses 'citation needed' where statements lack sources. High-quality articles clearly label contentious claims and provide multiple sourced perspectives. Anti-pattern: editorialising, advocacy without context, or leaving unsourced controversial assertions unmarked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of images, maps, and multimedia with informative captions
rubrics_metrics.description: Include photographs, maps, diagrams, and captions that add factual value (e.g., plant photos, memorials, schematic of chemical reaction), with source attributions and dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page includes images (plant, memorial, diagrams of reactions) and a coordinate map. Captions should state what is shown and when. Avoid using emotive images without explanatory context; ensure media are properly licensed and sourced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured sections and supplementary material (References, Further reading, External links)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organise content into logical sections (Background, Leak, Immediate aftermath, Subsequent legal action, Long-term effects, Environmental rehabilitation, Health care, Further reading, References, External links).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article demonstrates a standard structure for disaster coverage and provides extensive references, further reading, and external links. Good practice: include investigative reports, peer-reviewed studies, and primary documents. Anti-pattern: missing references section or burying key sources in prose without proper citations.
